acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Ira talks to Pablo Torre about Major League Baseball’s new challenge system, and how it’s been optimized for maximum drama.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Writer Jiayang Fan wrestles with a very common question she has never quite understood.
acts.credits: By Jiayang Fan; Produced by Diane Wu
acts.title: A Most American Question

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: People come from all over the country to walk down one of Michigan’s tallest sand dunes, and then promptly turn around and trudge back up. Aviva DeKornfeld talks to Americans spending their limited vacation time on this punishing activity.
acts.credits: By Aviva DeKornfeld; Produced by Molly Marcello
acts.title: City on a Hill of Sand

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Emanuele Berry talks to Ira about Season 13 of the reality TV show, Survivor, known to fans as the “race war” season.
acts.title: Cooked Island

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
Years before his famous dictionary, Noah Webster wrote a book that took on a life of its own and served an unexpected purpose.
A version of this story originally aired on the new 99 Percent Invisible and BBC series, A History of the United States in 100 Objects.
acts.credits: By Roman Mars; Produced by Emmanuel Dzotsi
acts.title: The Most American Schoolbook

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Emmanuel Dzotsi investigates a musical phenomenon very particular to the United States: singers embellishing the end of the national anthem.
acts.title: Jose Can You See?
